cb1551.q: A 29-year-old woman with a pituitary microadenoma has been receiving cabergoline 1 mg per week. She presents at 12 weeks of gestation. What is the most appropriate management? (Q-39909950) develop
o: Advise termination of pregnancy as cabergoline was continued during the first trimester
Follow up with serum prolactin levels monthly
Perform MRI of the sella to look for tumor enlargement
Reassure the patient and evaluate further only if symptoms such as headache or visual disturbance
cb1551.ex: Prolactin-secreting pituitary microadenomas (microprolactinomas) are commonly treated with dopamine agonists such as cabergoline or bromocriptine, which suppress prolactin secretion and shrink the **tumor**. Management during pregnancy: * Once pregnancy is confirmed, dopamine agonists are usually discontinued in patients with microadenomas. * The risk of **tumor** enlargement during pregnancy is very low (\~2–3%) for microadenomas. * Routine MRI or prolactin monitoring is not recommended, because prolactin levels naturally rise during pregnancy and do not correlate with **tumor** size.
